1) a small manually constructed dictionary of emotion-provoking event can be created through a survey of a few subjects; 2) a simple extension to the baseline approach using seed expansion and cluster-based aggregation can improve the quality of the automatically-acquired event dictionary; and 3) a simple evaluation of the quality of the event dictionary can be performed by using the dictionary to generate emotion-provoking sentences.

(1) we created a small manually-annotated event dictionary, (2) we evaluated several methods for automatically acquiring events and found that the best method is to use seed expansion and then perform clustering on the results, and (3) we found that the best evaluation method is to compare the automatically acquired events to the manually-constructed dictionary.

(1) the manual creation of a small dictionary of emotion-provoking event types is a feasible task, and can provide a useful basis for further research; (2) the automatic aggregation of events using web data is a feasible task; and (3) the proposed evaluation metrics are useful for evaluating the quality of the automatically acquired events.
